div.l: His resoıı̄uns he spak / ful solempnely
Shewynge alway / the encres of his wynnynge
He wolde the see were kept for eny thynge
Bitwixe Middelburgh and orwelle
Wel cowde he in eschaunge sheeldes selle
This worthy man / ful wel his witte bisette
Ther wiste no wight / that he was in dette
So estately was he of his goủernaıı̄unce
What with his bargeynes / and with his cheuissance
For sothe he was a worthy man with alle
But sothely to seyn / I noot how men hym calle
A Clerk ther was of Oxenforde of Oxenforde also
That vn to logike / longe tyme hadde I go
As lene was his hors / as is a rake
And he nas not right fat I vndertake
But loked holwe / and ther to sobirly
Ful thredbare was his oủerest courtepy
For he hadde geten hym / no benfice
Ne was so worldly / for to haue office
For hym was leuere / haue at his beddes hede
Twenty bokes / clad in blak or rede
Of Aristotil and his philosophie
Than robes riche fithel or gay sawtrie
But al be that he was a philosophre
Ȝit hadde he but lytel gold in cofre
But al that he myghte / of his frendes hente
On bokes and on lernynge he it spente
And besily gan for the soules preye
Of hem that hym ȝaue wherwith to scoleye
Of studie toke he most cure and hede
Nought oo word spak he more than was nede
And that was sayd in forme and reủerence
And short and quik / and ful of high sentence
Sownynge in moral v̉ertue / was his speche
And gladly wolde he lerne / and gladly teche
A Sergeant of the lawe war and wys
That ofte hadde ben at Parvys
That was also ful riche of excellence
Discrete he was / and of greet reủerence
